title: Can you guys recommend me some solid Forest Whitaker movies? I feel like I’ve only seen him in small roles and am always floored by his acting.

commenti.body:
I’m a huge fan of Ghost Dog: Way of the Samurai. Granted his performance is very subdued, as it’s Jarmusch, but can’t go wrong with a quirky movie about a mafia hitman who
lives by the Samurai code, with a score by The RZA.

He’s also got a big role in some of the middle seasons of The Shield.
Seconding this. Also his Oscar-winning role in *The Last King of Scotland*.

He's standout in his scene with Paul Newman in The Color of Money. Bird is a must-see for multiple reasons, but his performance is fantastic. I liked him in Smoke, a very underrated film. Ghost Dog and Last King of Scotland were mentioned. Recently, he was excellent in Godfather of Harlem.
This has been in my queue for way too long. Need to finally go for it.

well he won Best Actor for **Last King of Scotland** so I'd start there. 

Then maybe **Lee Daniel's The Butler**

**The Crying Game** is a supporting role but he's very memorable in it.
Oh hell Ya, Forrest was Bushido.
Not a movie but a TV series: ***Godfather of Harlem.*** It’s a pretty good and entertaining organized crime drama with only minor flaws. I legit binged it last month solely to see more Forrest.
Never heard of this, will track it down, thanks!
I watched on Hulu. It’s available on a few different services. Three seasons so far.

The Crying Game (1992). I actually had to pause the film check IMDB to verify the cast as I couldn’t believe it was a young FW. 

This is a really good film. Neil Jordan is a brilliant  writer and director, I recommend Mona Lisa (1986) to everyone. 

Ghost Dog is excellent too.

A movie often overlooked is Bird. Directed by Clint Eastwood and about the life of musician Charlie Parker.

Forrest Whitaker’s performance is strong and the film is overall pretty decent. 

Also love Ghost Dog but see that mentioned already. 

Movies where he isn’t the lead - The Crying Game

I think the argument can be made that he is the lead character in Bloodsport. If he had managed to get Jean-Claude Van Damme’s character back to USA, it would be a very different film.

But seriously, check out Lush Life with him and Jeff Goldblum, very good jazz movie.

Bloodsport is legit one of my favorite movies, I probably watch it at least once a year. 

It is very dumb, but it is very good.
It’s a fun flick, but I’m always astounded at how poorly acted the fight scenes are. It looks faker than pro wrestling.
I would be so fucking hyped if that’s true, but the only articles on it are from 2017.
You mean people don’t just stand there letting you repeatedly spin-kick them in the face in real life? Have you even been in a fight?
I’m saying even by action/martial arts movie standards, it’s very badly done

Yeah, I get what you’re saying. I’ve been watching that movie multiple times a year since it came out on video in the late 80s. I have no idea why it’s so beloved. It really is terrible, but we love it. I think if you saw it as a kid without a lot to compare it to it holds a place in your heart forever.
I did watch it many times as a kid and it does hold a place in my heart forever. I practically know the entire script by heart.

Just curious what you think has really good fight choreography. For me, The Raid: Redemption is just so amazing that it kind of ruins everything else. I think Ong Bak is pretty great and the first two Ip Man movies, early Jackie Chan is fun, but that’s about it for me these days.

I grew up with Ghost Dog getting played at least once a month by my brothers. He was a staple in my house. Additional small role in ensemble, Smoke. It is one of my favorite movies and his performance always gets me. Plus great stuff from Harvey Keitel and William Hurt

They've already been mentioned here so I'm just going to double (triple) down on Last King of Scotland and Crying Game. He's just phenomenal in both.

Just an obligatory warning for Last King of Scotland – it's not for the faint hearted. There are some pretty disturbing sequences.

I echo everyone on *The Crying Game, Bird*, and *The Last King of Scotland.* He's not a lead in *Crying Game*, but his character is absolutely pivotal and memorable.

In addition to what everyone else mentions, Forest is a wonderful character in *Phenomenon* as the main character's best friend, and he's also terrific in  supporting roles in *Panic Room* and *Rogue One* (and if you like that, he also reprises that role a few times in the fantastic series "Andor"), really fun in a goofy sci-fi movie *Species* (it's a silly movie but has a phenomenal cast), and great on "The Shield."

He's also got a fun small role in the superb film *Arrival*.

He’s a main character in season 5 of the shield, which is the best season and he is wonderful in it. The whole show is great, but if you just want to watch season 5 for him you can probably do it without being too lost

Ghost Dog: Way of the Samurai from Jim Jarmusch and Bird where he plays Charlie Parker, directed by Clint Eastwood. Both feature great performances from Forest Whitaker. Also both from very good directors.

While not a lead, his character is present throughout the campy wonder that is *Species* from 1995. With monster design by H.R. Geiger and an ensemble cast, there are many things to like about this. However, the unevenness of the film overall makes it 'only' a great sci fi and not an all time classic. An underrated film, I think, but stay far away from the sequels.
The driving scenes with the soundtrack background absolutely imprinted themselves on my teenage brain, directly into my long-term memory.
